newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL overnight rate flip-flops in wide range.
newsitem.headline: KL overnight rate flip-flops in wide range.

text.p: The overnight interbank rate fluctuated in a wide range as many players who had covered long-term earlier bid lower, dealers said on Tuesday.
It traded between 7.0 percent and 8.5 percent. At 0800 GMT, it was at 7.5/8.0 percent, they said.
"The market is short on the whole, but after the sharp rise in one-week rate, there is less interest in the overnight," said a dealer with a Malaysian bank.
One foreign bank dealer said some foreign banks, which are normally lenders, were also running short.
One-week money rose to 7.8/8.0 percent against 7.4/5 percent on Monday.
Two-week money was at 7.40/50 percent against 7.35/40 and three-week at 7.35/40 percent against 7.30/35.
One-month money was at 7.40 percent against 7.35, while three-month at 7.35/40 and six-month at 7.40/45 were both unchanged.
Earlier, short-term interbank rates rose further as people tried to book funds in anticipation of further tightening of the market over the next few days.
Dealers said the market would tighten after an outflow of one billion ringgit on Wednesday for two Bank Negara bill issues against a maturity of 500 million ringgit.
Dealers were divided over the possible trend in the domestic money market. But they agreed that if there was a flow of funds out of Malaysia, interest rates could be pushed up.
Last week, Bank Negara intervened to slow the ringgit's fall by selling nearly $200 million, dealers said. A 500-million ringgit Bank Negara bill issue also reduced liquidity in the flush market.
"With ringgit still under pressure to weaken, and stock market in the doldrums, there is bound to be more funds going out of Malaysia," said a dealer with a Malaysian bank.
Such fund outflows would push up domestic rates, he said.
Reflecting the trend, interest rate futures on the Malaysia Monetary Exchange were lower towards the close.
At 0820 GMT, three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate-based (KLIBOR) June contract fell one point to 92.68, or an implied yield of 7.32 percent.
September was down one point to 92.67, or 7.33 percent and December eased three points to 92.60, or 7.40 percent.
March 1998 contract fell three points to 92.50 and June two points to 92.48.
